CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who injured his right elbow approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He reports that his 13-year-old son was checking him several times with a lacrosse stick, which may have caused the injury. Patient denies falling. He describes the pain as sharp and localized to the tip of the elbow, with radiation down the forearm. Pain occurs with any movement of the elbow. He tried ibuprofen for a couple of days, which provided some relief. Patient reports usually forgetting to take medications for the pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. Lungs are clear bilaterally. Heart exam shows a grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur, which is known to the patient.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus type 2
Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2 out of 6)

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has two children, ages 13 and 10. Plays lacrosse with his children. Family follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. During the pandemic, patient noted he had fallen off from his diet but has since returned to compliance.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right elbow: Pain to palpation of the olecranon area of the posterior elbow. Mild pain with flexion and extension. Normal range of motion. Mild swelling and bruising noted. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart exam with grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur. No chest or abdominal tenderness on examination.

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: No fracture, no bony abnormality. Normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion from blunt trauma secondary to lacrosse stick contact. Patient prescribed ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and swelling. Ice elbow three times daily for 20 minutes at a time. Avoid playing lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow healing. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension management. Continue metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes management. Obtain A1C level to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment is needed in the future.
